title: Who can help with change
subject: RSHE
outcome: Identify who helps me through change.
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
source_note: Outcome and row reference supplied verbatim in the owner's Week 5 brief. Accepted Week 4 supplies format only. The underlying workbook was not reopened in this return; no independent cell check or source hash is claimed.

circle.title: Circle of support
circle.note: A circle of support is a group of people who can help. Use adults you know and trust. The same kind of help can come from more than one person. These are examples. A role does not mean you must trust that person.

sort.instruction: Match each role card to a kind of help. Use the made-up examples. More than one safe match may fit. Say, point or use your usual aid. Sort on the table or note the match in your book.
help_cards: Help get kit ready at home.
Try the first class step with the pupil.
Show the steps for a new club task.

sample_matches.help: Help get kit ready at home.
Try the first class step with the pupil.
Show the steps for a new club task.

sort.marking: These are sample fits, not fixed job limits. Accept any safe match with a sensible context or explanation. For the school story a teacher or teaching assistant is a clear fit. A parent/carer may help get kit ready; a familiar club leader is a separate community example, not required in the classroom story.

scene: A pupil has a new start to class. First they put their book on the table. Then they look at the first task. They are not sure what comes next.

model.sentence: The pupil could ask a teaching assistant to show the next step.
model.fade: First show the helper and kind of help. Then leave the helper choice to the pupil while the bank, starter and visible model remain. Next ask the pupil to choose how that adult could help.

privacy_pupil: Use the made-up story in class. For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. You can pass, point or ask for help.

private_card.title: My circle
private_card.instruction: Fill this card in private. Use roles, not names. You can write, draw or point. Keep this card.
private_card.help: You may leave any space blank. Not sure who could help? Ask for help in private. You do not need a role in each space.
private_card.note: Do not show this card to the group. An adult can help if you want.

safeguarding: If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult or support in any area, support them privately and do not press them. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept any blank space, a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, the private card, a book task or shared learning evidence. Do not read private cards aloud, collect or photograph them for assessment. Staff may support completion only with pupil agreement; the pupil keeps the card.
support_route: Use adults the pupil knows and trusts, including a familiar community role where appropriate. Do not instruct pupils to approach an unfamiliar adult alone. Use agreed home/school routes for help. A role title is a possible starting point, not a guarantee of safe support. No pupil has to endorse any adult or fill all three areas. If an adult is busy or the first response does not help, support asking another trusted adult.
practice_rule: All class prompts, sorting and explanation use made-up examples and the invented class-routine scene. No learner has to describe a real change, relationship or worry. Choose a helper role and match a kind of help by speaking, pointing, usual communication aid, drawing or faithful scribe/readback. A pass/observer option is valid; record learning not observed rather than failure. Do not use or collect the private card as evidence.
independence: Normal word bank, sentence starter, visible model, role/help cards and usual aids stay on all routes. Independent means the learner chooses a suitable helper role and kind of help for the invented change after a general task cue, without adult next-step content prompts. A faithful scribe/voicing of the learner's exact choice is access, not an adult-generated answer. Record mode and prompts precisely. The objective is identification, not independent spoken performance or real-life help-seeking.

routes.Supported: Keep all Level 2 aids. Teach one match, then offer two role/help choices and return the choice to the pupil. Reduced repetitions and faithful scribe/pointing available. Record content prompts.
routes.Independent: Keep all Level 2 aids and usual access. After a general cue, learner chooses a suitable role and how they could help the invented pupil. Log next-step content prompts separately.
routes.Aspire: Keep all Level 2 aids. Suggest another safe helper or a second kind of help if the first adult is busy. A plausible alternative context is welcome. Extra writing and personal disclosure are not required.

success: Choose a safe helper role for the story.
Show a kind of help that fits.
Show another safe way to get help if needed.
timing: 0–3 calm story starter; 3–7 support circle roles; 7–11 model helper and help; 11–12 reset.
12–17 role/help sort; 17–20 private hinge; 20–24 plan who could help and how; 24–25 reset.
25–33 individual story choices and brief check; 33–36 private My circle card; 36–38 next step and response; 38–40 private exit.

scaffolds.model: The pupil could ask a teacher.
A teaching assistant could show the next step.
A parent or carer could help get kit ready.
The pupil could choose a teacher to show the steps.
They could ask a teaching assistant to show the next step.

scaffolds.start: In the story, ... could help by ... .
scaffolds.model: In the story, a teacher could help by showing the steps.
Another helper could be a teaching assistant.

hinge.question: The pupil needs the new class steps. Which help fits?
hinge.A: Ask a teacher to show the steps.
hinge.B: Ask for help with a different task only.
hinge.decision: Check privately using the invented scene. Accept usual pointing/words/aid and other sensible safe role/help combinations. If A or a suitable alternative with a clear fit, proceed. If B, unclear or no response, re-model role plus relevant help, reduce to two choices and use parallel check. A pass is not evidence of misunderstanding.

parallel.question: The pupil needs to try the first class step. Which help fits?
parallel.B: Ask a teaching assistant to try the first step with them.

misconceptions: Each role can give only one kind of help.
Cards are examples. More than one adult can listen, explain or show a step. Accept sensible safe matches for the context.
A role title means the pupil must trust that adult or fill every part of the circle.
Use a trusted adult and usual safe routes. No learner must endorse an adult or show support in all three areas. Any space can stay blank; support privately, never press.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: One mild scene, small card set, read-aloud and explicit modelling; reduce to two choices, fade adult content prompts while retaining aids. Repeat a short relevant match.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Wait time, pointing or usual aid, exact scribe/voicing and readback. Do not require eye contact or speech. Confirm the pupil's own helper and help choices.
adaptations.SEMH: Predictable story-only class work; no public personal questions or comparison of support circles. Pass, observer option, quiet pause and supported return. Do not ask pupils to explain a pass.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Usual safe seating, accessible print, reachable sort cards and normal communication aids; quiet reset without sudden sound or forced movement.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Explain role, help, change and community using short examples; allow usual language support and exact selected wording.

cold_call_label: Optional private fictional check prompts; never public personal questions.

cold_call.F: Which role could help the story pupil?
cold_call.M: What could that adult do to help?
cold_call.H: Which other safe helper could fit if that adult is busy?

ta_focus.I_do: Model a role plus a relevant kind of help. Check one selection privately, keeping bank/starter/model visible.
ta_focus.We_do: Read the sort cards, accept sensible alternative matches and give wait time. Support two-choice matching then return the choice.
ta_focus.Independent: Check the invented helper/how choices in usual mode, logging access and content prompts. Private My circle card is optional, stays with pupil and is not evidence. Route concerns through safeguarding.

prompt_ladder: Point to the place or instruction.
Model the first step only, then return the task.
evidence: Use Evidence Sheet for anonymous/session learning notes: helper role and relevant kind of help chosen for the invented change; an alternative safe helper if offered; usual mode, access and adult content prompts; one NS and learner response. Do not record personal roles from My circle, names, relationships or worries. Observed with content prompts, observed without next-step content prompts and learning not observed remain distinct. Identification can be shown by selecting or pointing; no independent speech or real-life help-seeking claim.
marking: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.
where_this_leads: This helps me find safe help when I learn a new task or do a job.

paragraphs: Identify who helps me through change.
Use the made-up story in class. For real help, ask a trusted adult in private. You can pass, point or ask for help.
A pupil has a new start to class. First they put their book on the table. Then they look at the first task. They are not sure what comes next.
Pick a role that could help the story pupil. Show what that adult could do. You can point, say, draw or use your usual aid. A scribe can write your words and read them back.
The pupil could ask a teaching assistant to show the next step.
Start: In the story, ... could help by ... .
Model: In the story, a teacher could help by showing the steps.
Keep your first try. Use one next step. Reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. You can pass or watch, then come back with help.
My circle is for you to keep. Use roles, not names. Any space can stay blank. Ask for help in private. Do not put your own card choices or real worries in class work.
Use a work code, not a name. Log the made-up task. Keep real worries, names and roles from My circle out of this sheet. Use the school’s own safe record for real concerns.

States: chose with no step cues; chose with step cues; learning not seen this time. A step cue tells what to choose next. Log words, point, draw, aid or exact scribe/TA voice. The aim is to choose who and how. No speech test. An adult-picked answer is not the pupil’s own choice.

No adult to choose? Give help in private. Do not press. Any card space can stay blank. If a pupil shares a real worry, pass it to the safeguarding lead. Use the school route. Listen and give calm support. Do not probe or promise to keep a secret. Keep real details out of this pack and shared work.
E: real work saved. R: only with Voice, Audience, one NS and a reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio.

The pupil selects a helper and the relevant kind of help. An exact point or selection is valid. Re-model if the link is unclear. A pass remains unobserved, not a wrong answer. Do not substitute a real personal change.

The pupil needs the new class steps. Which help fits? Correct A: Ask a teacher to show the steps. Check privately using the invented scene. Accept usual pointing/words/aid and other sensible safe role/help combinations. If A or a suitable alternative with a clear fit, proceed. If B, unclear or no response, re-model role plus relevant help, reduce to two choices and use parallel check. A pass is not evidence of misunderstanding.
The pupil needs to try the first class step. Which help fits? Correct B: Ask a teaching assistant to try the first step with them. Recheck privately with normal aids and usual mode.

Normal word bank, sentence starter, visible model, role/help cards and usual aids stay on all routes. Independent means the learner chooses a suitable helper role and kind of help for the invented change after a general task cue, without adult next-step content prompts. A faithful scribe/voicing of the learner's exact choice is access, not an adult-generated answer. Record mode and prompts precisely. The objective is identification, not independent spoken performance or real-life help-seeking.

Chose role and relevant help without adult next-step content prompts; Chose role and help with adult content prompts; Learning not observed this time. Record choices, mode, aids and all content prompts. A scribe/TA voicing exact selected words is access; an adult-generated choice is supported teaching.
Each role can give only one kind of help. Cards are examples. More than one adult can listen, explain or show a step. Accept sensible safe matches for the context.

A role title means the pupil must trust that adult or fill every part of the circle. Use a trusted adult and usual safe routes. No learner must endorse an adult or show support in all three areas. Any space can stay blank; support privately, never press.
Story starter. Bank: pupil, new, step, help. Start: The pupil could ask ... . Visible model: The pupil could ask a teacher.
Model check. Bank: adult, role, show, step. Start: They could help by ... . Visible model: A teaching assistant could show the next step.
Guided sort. Bank: home, school, club, help. Start: This role could ... . Visible model: A parent or carer could help get kit ready.
Private hinge. Bank: role, help, next, adult. Start: The pupil could choose ... . Visible model: The pupil could choose a teacher to show the steps.
Choose and plan. Bank: teacher, helper, show, try. Start: They could ask ... to ... . Visible model: They could ask a teaching assistant to show the next step.
Story choice and private card. Bank: role, help, blank, private. Start: In the story, ... could help by ... . Visible model: In the story, a teacher could help by showing the steps.
Feedback and exit. Bank: busy, next, help, adult. Start: Another helper could be ... . Visible model: Another helper could be a teaching assistant.

All routes keep banks, starters, models and normal aids. Teach a short match explicitly; reduce to two choices if needed. Give processing time and flexible grouping. Do not require speech or eye contact. Use agreed sensory/physical access and quiet resets. Plan in any language. Observer/pass and supported return remain.

If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult or support in any area, support them privately and do not press them. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept any blank space, a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, the private card, a book task or shared learning evidence. Do not read private cards aloud, collect or photograph them for assessment. Staff may support completion only with pupil agreement; the pupil keeps the card.

Keep only fictional role/help choices, relevant alternatives, access/prompts, one NS and the pupil’s reply. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.

BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 5 · formative
Theme Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Identify who helps me through change.
Source: BUILD Weekly Spring row 68, as supplied in the owner brief. The workbook was not reopened; no independent cell check is claimed.

Identify a possible helper by role and choose how that adult could help with an invented change. A home/school/community circle gives examples of support. A small role/help sort develops the link between a role and a useful kind of help. The private My circle card stays with the pupil and is not evidence.

Books; circle guide on Support Cards page 1; role/help sort on page 2; invented scene/model on page 3; private My circle card on page 4; seven aid sets on pages 5–6; vocabulary and private staff work note. Confirm usual communication, reading and physical access. Agree safe home/school help routes. No personal change or support-circle questions.
This helps me find safe help when I learn a new task or do a job.
Chunks last 12, 13 and 15 minutes. Two one-minute resets are inside the 40 minutes. Reduce repetitions for access. Pass, observer and supported return remain available.

0–3: read the calm new-class-routine story; ask which role could help. 3–7: use the home/school/community guide. Roles are examples, not proof that an adult is trusted. 7–11: model a helper and relevant help, then privately check one selection. 11–12: quiet reset with usual access.

12–17: sort four roles and four kinds of help. Read cards aloud. Accept more than one sensible safe match; cards do not define fixed job limits. 17–20: main hinge A and parallel B. 20–24: choose a helper role and plan how they could help the invented pupil. 24–25: quiet reset.

25–33: check individual who/how choices for the invented change, with banks/starters/models and usual aids. 33–36: offer optional private My circle completion, only with agreed support; pupil keeps it. 36–38: set one next step and invite a response. 38–40: private story exit. Do not collect private-card content.
Keep all Level 2 aids. Teach one match, then offer two role/help choices and return the choice to the pupil. Reduced repetitions and faithful scribe/pointing available. Record content prompts.
Keep all Level 2 aids and usual access. After a general cue, learner chooses a suitable role and how they could help the invented pupil. Log next-step content prompts separately.

Keep all Level 2 aids. Suggest another safe helper or a second kind of help if the first adult is busy. A plausible alternative context is welcome. Extra writing and personal disclosure are not required.

The pupil could ask a teaching assistant to show the next step. First show the helper and kind of help. Then leave the helper choice to the pupil while the bank, starter and visible model remain. Next ask the pupil to choose how that adult could help. Fade content prompts only. Keep all access aids in view. Record supported teaching and later chosen answers separately.

Identification may be shown by pointing, selecting, drawing, words or usual aid. A faithful scribe or TA can voice the pupil’s exact choice, read it back and permit correction. Record this access separately from adult-generated answers or next-step content prompts. There is no independent spoken-performance test.

I do: model role plus help. We do: read cards and accept safe alternative fits. Independent: check the fictional choices in usual mode. Keep My circle optional, private and outside evidence. Route any concern through safeguarding.
Level 2 word bank, sentence starter and visible model stay on every task and all routes. These seven sets also appear on Support Cards pages 5–6.
Model: The pupil could ask a teacher.
Model: A teaching assistant could show the next step.
Model: A parent or carer could help get kit ready.
Model: The pupil could choose a teacher to show the steps.
Model: They could ask a teaching assistant to show the next step.
Start: In the story, ... could help by ... .
Model: In the story, a teacher could help by showing the steps.
Model: Another helper could be a teaching assistant.

1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time. Log content prompts during observed choices separately from normal access.
Choose a safe helper role for the story.
Show a kind of help that fits.
Show another safe way to get help if needed.
Select the model helper and kind of help in usual mode. Re-model if needed. Use the story only. A pass is not a wrong answer.

Main A fits: ask a teacher to show the steps. B gives help for a different task only. Check privately in usual mode. Accept relevant safe alternatives. If wrong or unclear, re-model, offer two choices and use the parallel. A pass remains unobserved.
To try the first step, B fits: ask a teaching assistant to try it with the pupil. A hides the steps. Recheck privately with normal aids.
One mild scene, small card set, read-aloud and explicit modelling; reduce to two choices, fade adult content prompts while retaining aids. Repeat a short relevant match.
Wait time, pointing or usual aid, exact scribe/voicing and readback. Do not require eye contact or speech. Confirm the pupil's own helper and help choices.
Predictable story-only class work; no public personal questions or comparison of support circles. Pass, observer option, quiet pause and supported return. Do not ask pupils to explain a pass.
Usual safe seating, accessible print, reachable sort cards and normal communication aids; quiet reset without sudden sound or forced movement.
Plan in any language. Explain role, help, change and community using short examples; allow usual language support and exact selected wording.
Use fictional checks only; allow pointing or pass. F: Which role could help the story pupil? M: What could that adult do to help? H: Which other safe helper could fit if that adult is busy?

Each role can offer more than one kind of help; accept sensible safe matches. A role title does not prove trust or oblige a pupil to fill every circle area. Any space may stay blank. Give private support without pressing.

If a pupil cannot identify a trusted adult or support in any area, support them privately and do not press them. Offer a familiar school role and help make contact through the school route; accept any blank space, a blank card or pass. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Do not write disclosure details in this pack, the private card, a book task or shared learning evidence. Do not read private cards aloud, collect or photograph them for assessment. Staff may support completion only with pupil agreement; the pupil keeps the card.

Use adults the pupil knows and trusts, including a familiar community role where appropriate. Do not instruct pupils to approach an unfamiliar adult alone. Use agreed home/school routes for help. A role title is a possible starting point, not a guarantee of safe support. No pupil has to endorse any adult or fill all three areas. If an adult is busy or the first response does not help, support asking another trusted adult.

Use the invented change only. Keep cards, banks, starters, models and usual aids. The objective is identifying helper and help, not speech or personal disclosure. Record exact choices, access and adult content prompts. Pass/observer is valid; do not infer real-life help-seeking.

Use Evidence Sheet for anonymous/session learning notes: helper role and relevant kind of help chosen for the invented change; an alternative safe helper if offered; usual mode, access and adult content prompts; one NS and learner response. Do not record personal roles from My circle, names, relationships or worries. Observed with content prompts, observed without next-step content prompts and learning not observed remain distinct. Identification can be shown by selecting or pointing; no independent speech or real-life help-seeking claim.

Chose role and relevant help without adult next-step content prompts; Chose role and help with adult content prompts; Learning not observed this time. A faithful scribe records the learner’s exact choice. An adult-chosen answer is supported teaching, not the learner’s own selection.

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping.

Use books or normal aids for invented matches and who/how choices. The private My circle card is an intentional fill-in exception. No personal names, private-card roles or real concerns in class work, photographs or shared evidence. Plan in any language.
Week 5 is formative; Week 6 is assessing. Only Week 5 is authored here. The owner supplies row 68 and the exact outcome; identifying source labels are rendered generically.
